violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: orange and yellow ramen broth on stove 125,130f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. CDI reheated to 165f

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed fish in reduced oxygen packaging thawing in packaging on the counter
violations.corrective_action: ROP fish must thaw outside of the packaging under refrigeration. CDI package opened and thawing in the refrigerator

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 2 door prep cooler broken. Observed ice buckets inside. Food 42-49f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI food discarded after 4 hours.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: cooked potatoes and French toast with egg batter on counter on time control without time mark
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. CDI, time marked.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: cool chopped lettuce and tomato in shallow containers without the lid on, recommend adding ice to containers. These items must cool to 41f in 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI ice added and lids removed Eggs & Sushi (Inspection Date: 04/13/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: white powders in large plastic containers in dry storage shelf without label.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CDI labeled

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Coffee bags stored on the floor under equipment drying rack.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. CDI moved to clean/dry shelf

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw thawing tuna over lettuce and eggs over lettuce and tomatoes in refrigerators.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI moved.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: Chemical sanitizer immersion time was not adequate for bleach sanitizing solution. Observed PIC cut open raw tuna package, wash knife with soap, and return to storage bin without using a sanitizer step.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. CDI sanitized in bleach for 10 seconds.

violations.title: Food Contact Surface, 4 Hour Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed sushi cutting boards and knives located at the prep line that are not being cleaned at least every 4 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils must be cleaned and sanitized at least every 4 hours to prevent contamination by bacterial growth. CDI cleaned and sanitized with bleach Eggs & Sushi (Inspection Date: 10/16/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. Observed Windex stored on sushi prep table. PIC said its used to clean the sushi display case and equipment.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. CDI Windex removed. Use approved food contact surfaces to clean equipment, such as bleach and quaternary ammonium.

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: Observed medicine bottles and toe nail clippers stored in such a way that they could contaminate food at the cook line and sushi station.
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. CDI items removed from prep table.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed reduced oxygen packaged fish thawing inside original packaging.
violations.corrective_action: Fish frozen in reduced oxygen packaging must be removed during thawing process. CDI plastic packaging was cut to allow air/oxygen inside.

violations.title: Equipment Clean to Sight and Touch
violations.observation: Encrusted grease deposits and/or other soil deposits were observed on the food contact surfaces of the following cooking equipment: back wall/shelves of refrigerator #1 covered in brown residue.
violations.corrective_action: The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. A surface that is soiled cannot be effectively sanitized. CDI cleaned
